title: Packages and services
summary: No internet, two .deb files and a dependency puzzle. Query packages with dpkg, install offline, configure a service, start it, check it listens with ss, and make it start at boot.

nodes.jaffa: a new server with no internet access; packages wait in /root/packages

tasks.title: Whose file is this?
tasks.text: Every file the system installed belongs to a package. Which package installed `/usr/bin/ssh-keygen`?
hints: `dpkg -S <path>` searches the installed packages' file lists. (On Red Hat family systems it is `rpm -qf <path>`.)

tasks.title: Read the label first
tasks.text: Ops dropped two packages in `/root/packages`. Before installing anything, read its label: `sprinkles-cli` **depends** on `netcat-openbsd` and on one other package. Which one?
hints: A `.deb` file carries its metadata (name, version, dependencies). `dpkg-deb --info file.deb` (or `-I`) shows it without installing.
Look at the `Depends:` line of `dpkg-deb -I /root/packages/sprinkles-cli_0.9.1_all.deb`. `dpkg-deb -c` lists the files inside.

answer_cmd.cmd: dpkg-deb -f /root/packages/sprinkles-cli_0.9.1_all.deb Depends | tr ',' '\n' | grep -v netcat | awk '{print $1}'

tasks.title: Install, offline
tasks.text: Install `sprinkles-cli` from `/root/packages`. This server has **no internet**, so apt can't download anything. Try installing it on its own first and read the error: it is a useful one. Then get it done.

checks.fail_msg: crumbd is not (fully) installed yet. Check: dpkg -l crumbd
sprinkles-cli is not (fully) installed yet. Check: dpkg -l sprinkles-cli (iU means unpacked but not configured).

hints: `dpkg -i /root/packages/sprinkles-cli_0.9.1_all.deb` complains that it depends on crumbd, which isn't installed. dpkg installs files, but never fetches dependencies.

Install both in one go: `dpkg -i /root/packages/*.deb`. Or let apt sort out the order from local files: `apt install /root/packages/*.deb` (the paths must start with `/` or `./`, so apt knows they are files).
Already ran the first command? Install crumbd, then `dpkg --configure -a` finishes the half-installed sprinkles-cli.

tasks.title: Where's the config?
tasks.text: What is the full path of the **configuration file** that the `crumbd` package installed?
hints: `dpkg -L crumbd` lists every file a package installed.
Configuration lives under `/etc` (and packages mark such files as *conffiles*, so upgrades don't overwrite your edits).

tasks.title: Configure and start
tasks.text: The company port plan says crumbd lives on **port {{PORT}}**. Configure it, then **start** the service and check that it is listening. `sprinkles` should then print a crumb of wisdom.

checks.fail_msg: The config file doesn't say port = {{PORT}} yet.
Nothing is listening on TCP port {{PORT}}. Is the service started (and restarted after the config change)?
sprinkles doesn't get an answer from crumbd.

hints: Change one line in place with `sed -i 's/^port = .*/port = {{PORT}}/' /etc/crumbd/crumbd.conf`. Look at the file before and after with `cat`.
The package installed a service script in `/etc/init.d/crumbd`. `service crumbd start` runs it (`status`, `stop` and `restart` work too). On a systemd machine you'd use `systemctl start crumbd`.
Is it listening? `ss -ltn` lists listening TCP sockets (`-l` listening, `-t` TCP, `-n` numbers, add `-p` for the process). If it didn't start, read `/var/log/crumbd.log`.

steps.cmd: sed -i 's/^port = .*/port = {{PORT}}/' /etc/crumbd/crumbd.conf && service crumbd restart && ss -ltn && sprinkles

tasks.title: Open for business, every boot
tasks.text: Two last things. crumbd only listens on `127.0.0.1`, so other machines can't reach it: make it listen on **all interfaces** (and restart it). And make sure it **starts at boot**: enable the service for the normal runlevels.

checks.fail_msg: crumbd isn't listening on all interfaces (0.0.0.0:{{PORT}}) yet. Check with: ss -ltn
crumbd is not enabled at boot (no S..crumbd link in /etc/rc2.d).

hints: `127.0.0.1` means "this machine only"; `0.0.0.0` means "every address this machine has". Change `listen` in the config, then `service crumbd restart`.
With SysV init scripts, "enabled" means a start link in `/etc/rc2.d` and friends. `update-rc.d crumbd defaults` creates them from the script's header. (systemd: `systemctl enable crumbd`.)

steps.cmd: sed -i 's/^listen = .*/listen = 0.0.0.0/' /etc/crumbd/crumbd.conf && service crumbd restart && update-rc.d crumbd defaults && ss -ltn
